predictiveVsCausal.languageRule: this pack writes 'association' for every measured coefficient; 'premium', 'effect' and 'sensitivity' appear only as quoted legacy language or as withdrawn claims
predictiveVsCausal.legacyDeltaR2: the legacy's CBD-only/CBD+MRT hierarchical regression is a predictive increment claim; its outputs (R² 0.2263 / 0.2341, delta +0.0078) are absent from this checkout and are not re-derived, so even the predictive-increment narrative cannot be re-measured here
predictiveVsCausal.statement: every coefficient in responses.specifications is a predictive association: transactions nearer a station differ in price, conditional on controls, in one cross-section. Nothing here identifies why — no instrument, no quasi-experiment, no pretrend design, no treatment assignment — so no coefficient supports a causal 'premium' claim.

reasons: control sets cannot be equalised: every condo row carries null lease commencement, null storey and null town, so the condo specification is strictly poorer than the HDB rich specification
response variances differ (recorded per specification as sdLogResponse) and standardized betas are scale facts of their own samples, not effect sizes comparable across samples
the condo sample mixes ECs with condominiums (ecShareOfSample is recorded per specification)
the area grain differs (HDB rich uses town FE; the common specification uses planning_area FE because condo rows carry no town)
both coefficients are conditional associations in one cross-section; neither is an effect, so a ratio of them is not a ratio of effects
nonComparability.statement: the standardized effects are reported as recorded fields and their ratio is computed, not asserted; the non-comparability reasons above are stated alongside, and no raw dollar-per-100m multiple between segments appears anywhere in this ledger
